description: Abwaab is a learning platform reimagining how students across MENA study, practice, and prepare for success. With 12 million downloads, over 500,000 subscriptions sold, and 1.5 billion minutes watched, Abwaab helps students in grades 7-12 master national curriculum content at their own pace affordably and accessible through short-form videos, assessments, and performance analytics.
founders: Hamdi Tabbaa, Hussein Al‑Sarabi, Sabri Hakim

description: Algebra AI designs, builds, and operates AI agent systems for mid-market businesses in the GCC. It is the first company BECO has co-founded and incubated. Rather than offering off-the-shelf software, Algebra AI embeds with each client, maps their existing workflows, and builds AI systems around how the business actually works. The same team that designs a system builds it, runs it, and stays accountable for it as the client’s business evolves.
founders: Anis Harb, BECO Capital, Infinity Constellation, Silicon Badia, Waseel Investments
co_investors: Infinity Constellation, Silicon Badia, Waseel Investments

description: Amaani is building the next generation of beauty and wellness brands from the Middle East. Its first brand, AÏZA, is a Dubai-based masstige beauty brand, combining prestige positioning with a mass market price point. Its “Past Forward” philosophy pairs regional ingredients, including dates, black seed, and bakhoor, with clinically proven actives, developed in specialist laboratories across Korea, Japan, and Italy. We met Shubham Poddar early on, when he was raising Amaani’s pre-seed round, and stayed close to the business from there. What stood out over time was Shubham’s ability to build and adapt quickly, while the business itself began showing clear signs of pull from both customers and retailers. His perspective was shaped by his years at Peak XV, formerly Sequoia India, working on D2C beauty investments including Mamaearth and Minimalist, paired with a team bringing deep operating experience from L’Oréal, Huda Beauty, Elizabeth Arden, and Careem.

Bayzat began as a digital health insurance platform, helping businesses compare and manage employee benefits. By listening to customer feedback, they expanded into payroll and HR software, ultimately evolving into an all-in-one platform that powers HR, payroll, benefits, performance management, and more for thousands of businesses across MENA.

description: BRKZ is a managed B2B marketplace modernizing how contractors source, finance, and receive building materials. Buyers place orders through BRKZ’s digital platform, which fulfills them by sourcing competitively from the supplier side of the marketplace, bringing transparency, faster delivery, and tailored financing to a sector long defined by manual workflows and fragmentation. Prior to partnering, we had been tracking BRKZ since their inception. The company aligned closely with our Construction Tech thesis, mirroring the evolution we saw in PropTech a decade prior, where base-layer digital marketplaces became integral to the industry before enabling innovative offshoots like embedded financing. Today, BRKZ is a disciplined, high-growth operation with a strong team. The company is scaling revenues while maintaining margins, and is on track to become the construction operating system for the region.

Careem began as a corporate car booking platform. Having initially started as a B2B service, Careem soon became the MENA’s leading ride-hailing app, scaling to over 70 cities across 10+ countries and raising over $700 million in funding. From our very first meeting, Mudassir and Magnus displayed a high degree of self awareness combined with intellect and urgency. They have since paved the way and inspired many others to build from the region showing what’s possible when local insight meets global execution.

Chatfood was a platform that enabled users to place direct orders with restaurants through social channels like WhatsApp and Instagram. Recognizing the region’s rapid growth in the FoodTech space and with aggregators scaling dramatically, we were drawn by the opportunity to partner with Chatfood.

ClearGrid is a digital debt resolution platform rethinking how consumer collections are done across MENA, by bringing a tech-first, borrower-centric approach to a space traditionally known for opacity and unpleasant borrower experience. Through modern UX, machine learning, and empathetic communication, the platform helps lenders boost recoveries up to 25% more than traditional peers while providing borrowers with a more compassionate experience.
founders: Mohammad Al Zaben, Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, Mohammad Al Khalili
co_investors: Endeavor Catalyst, Raed Ventures, Jason Gardner (Marqeta CEO), Amjad Masad (Replit CEO)

description: CoinMENA is a crypto-first digital assets platform founded in the UAE, licensed by both the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority in Dubai and the Central Bank of Bahrain. CoinMENA makes it simple and secure for consumers and enterprises to buy, sell, and store crypto assets while depositing and withdrawing in local currency. We were drawn to the founders’ early conviction, technical depth, and deep ties to the region’s crypto ecosystem. Together, they’ve built CoinMENA into one of the region’s most credible and compliant exchanges. The team has also created a resilient underlying business that supported their mission through challenging periods for the sector. As they expand into staking, payments, and credit, CoinMENA is building the foundation for a broader crypto-financial stack in the region.
founders: Talal Tabbaa, Dina Sam’an, Yazan Barghuthi

description: Compedica is a medical device company on a mission to transform how diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are treated, operating in the UK and the UAE. The company has developed PulseFlowDF, an FDA and CE-approved wearable therapy system that combines mobile offloading, blood flow stimulation, and compliance monitoring into a single, user-friendly device. DFUs are one of the most debilitating and costly complications of diabetes, often leading to infection and amputation. With over 425 million people globally living with diabetes, and 34% facing a lifetime risk of developing a DFU, the clinical and economic burden is massive. Compedica’s innovation addresses this by enabling patients to heal at home without sacrificing mobility, offering a solution that is clinically effective and cost effective for health systems.
founders: Jim Mellon, Jamie Gibson, Daniel Blackman

description: DTEK is reimagining in-store retail, leveraging proprietary AI and computer vision to optimize store operations, reduce queue times, and improve the overall shopping experience through a purpose built self checkout till. Their flagship solution, SWIFT, identifies grocery items in under 200 milliseconds and allows shoppers to complete checkout in under 30 seconds, enhancing transaction efficiency and enabling stores to handle more customers effectively, especially during peak hours. DTEK partners with supermarkets, retailers, sports venues, and other businesses, to equip them with their self-checkout solution. The company initially began as a digital POS for grocers, scaling rapidly to meaningful ARR across 7 markets. Despite the company’s success, they pivoted to a stickier and more promising business model, solving their customers’ need for self-checkout tills. Since backing DTEK, the team have demonstrated the maturity and self-awareness that enables clear thinking and resilience in difficult decisions. This combination of technical execution and adaptability reflects the founder qualities we seek in building category-defining businesses.
founders: Sanad Yaghi, Shadi Ayoubi, Ali Al Sayegh

description: Ejari allows tenants to split their annual rent into monthly payments through a “Rent Now, Pay Later” (RNPL) model, tackling Saudi Arabia’s $35 billion residential leasing sector. The company addresses a fundamental pain point in the Saudi rental market, where tenants traditionally face the burden of paying rent in one or two large upfront checks. Using an on-demand subleasing structure, Ejari becomes the tenant on record and subleases to customers at a premium, while landlords receive their full payment upfront. When we met the team, we had already built conviction in the RNPL opportunity through our PropTech investment thesis. After several in-depth conversations with the Ejari team, we were compelled by their combined expertise in real estate, banking, and technology – all core skillsets required for such a business – and ended up leading their seed round.
founders: Yazeed Alshamsi, Mohammed AlKhelewy, Fahad Albedah, and Khalid AlMunif

description: FlapKap is a tech-enabled SME lender that provides fast, flexible, and data-driven working capital to both online and offline businesses across Egypt and the UAE, with plans to expand further across the Gulf. The company turns around loan offers in under 48 hours and maintains healthy default rates through proprietary underwriting and smart repayment structures. Today, FlapKap is scaling a capital-efficient model built for the region’s underserved $50B TAM. Given our high conviction in the SME lending space, we had met many tackling the same opportunity. None impressed us more than Coucha and his team. We partnered with FlapKap at the seed, drawn to their execution strength and financial discipline, reflected in strong unit economics that demonstrate a robust operational model. Coucha brings valuable entrepreneurial insight, having scaled Kijamii and experienced the same financing pain points FlapKap now solves. With an exceptionally strong founding team, early traction, and backing from global investors like QED, FlapKap is well-positioned to capture this market opportunity.
founders: Ahmad Coucha, Khaled Nassef, Sherif Bichara, Kunal Harisinghani

description: Initially founded in the UAE, Fresha is a global marketplace and software platform for beauty and wellness businesses, offering tools for appointments, payments, point-of-sale, and client marketing. The company set out to modernize a traditionally offline and underserved industry with intuitive, software-driven solutions. Today, Fresha powers over 130,000+ businesses in 120+ countries, with particular strength across Europe and emerging markets. We first partnered with William and Nick in 2017, drawn to their deep understanding of their customer base and product-led growth strategy. The founders built an exceptionally simple onboarding process that allowed low-tech salon owners to self-serve on basic scheduling tools. Once customers were engaged with the core product, Fresha gradually introduced additional features and value-added services while maintaining its foundational simplicity. This disciplined approach to product development, focused on single-unit salons as their ideal customer profile, enabled Fresha to scale globally while staying true to user needs. Fresha remains one of the region’s clearest examples of building a global business from the Gulf.
co_investors: General Atlantic, KKR, FJ Labs, Partech Ventures

description: Keyper is building a digital operating system for property in the UAE, with a focus on property management, brokerage and rent facilitation (RNPL).The platform’s RNPL offering helps tenants split payments into monthly installments and gives landlords access to upfront income, all through a mobile-first experience. With backing from Dubai Land Department, Keyper is creating the financial rails to simplify and scale real estate in the UAE.

Kitopi is a tech-enabled F&B operator that runs over 200 outlets, including both restaurants and delivery-only locations. With operations across the GCC, Kitopi has built end-to-end infrastructure, with an in-house suite of applications (known as SKOS) that allows them to maximize efficiency and increase utilization across all their kitchens whilst delivering a personalized experience to all diners.
founders: Mohamad Ballout, Saman Darkan, Bader Ataya, Andy Arenas, Sami Bejjani

description: Mango Sciences is a UAE and US based HealthTech company, building the world’s largest non-Caucasian oncology dataset while transforming access to precision medicine in emerging markets. Its AI-powered platform, Querent, enables real-world data applications across value-based financing, clinical trials, and drug development. We first invested in Mango Sciences, drawn by the uniqueness of the opportunity, the defensibility of the model, and the technical strength of the founding team. As pharma increasingly shifts toward data-driven, globally inclusive approaches, Mango Sciences is uniquely positioned to unlock innovation and value across the healthcare ecosystem. Through its proprietary dataset of 2.6 million patient lives and strategic partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies, the team is driving impact across clinical trial recruitment, real-world evidence and analytics, and value-based financing to expand access to cancer care.

Marti is Türkiye’s homegrown mobility platform, bringing accessible, tech-enabled transport options to urban riders. Marti began with e-scooters, expanded into ride-hailing, and today the Marti app offers a full stack of mobility services. In 2023, the company listed on the NYSE through a de-SPAC under the ticker MRT. As our only Türkiye investment, we were drawn to the founders’ clarity of vision and operational rigor, and alignment with our internal thesis and expertise on the mobility space from prior investments such as Careem. CEO
founders: Oğuz Alper Öktem, Sena Öktem, Cankut Durgun

description: MaxAB is a B2B e-commerce and FinTech platform digitizing the fragmented grocery supply chain, billing, and financing experience across the Middle East and Africa. The company streamlines procurement by connecting merchants directly to suppliers through a tech-enabled, end-to-end logistics network, and has since expanded into bill aggregation and embedded financing. We backed MaxAB at the Series A in 2019. The company scaled to serve over 150,000 merchants in Egypt and, in 2024, merged with Wasoko to form MaxSoko, the continent’s largest B2B retail platform, now supporting more than 300,000 merchants across the region.

Merkle Science is a cryptocurrency risk and forensics platform that helps exchanges, institutions, and regulators detect illicit activity on-chain. The company provides behavioral intelligence for blockchain compliance, including real-time transaction tracing, risk scoring, and smart contract forensics. Merkle operates globally with offices in the US, UK, India, and Singapore, serving over 70 clients. We backed Merkle at the Series A in 2022 as the company sought to target the UAE as a core market, given the rapidly maturing crypto regulatory landscape following the establishment of the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority. The company has since expanded from Asia into the US and Europe while building a differentiated product in a fast-moving category.

Myki was an offline-first password and identity manager. Designed with privacy-centric architecture, Myki stored credentials locally on user devices, never in the cloud, enabling frictionless logins and secure access for individuals and SMEs alike. The platform offered advanced 2FA, breach detection, and password-sharing tools, wrapped in an elegant mobile-first experience.

NorthLadder helps telcos, retailers, and phone makers get more value from used smartphones by making the trade-in and resale process faster, simpler, and more cost-effective. In a $75 billion market expected to reach $200 billion by 2033, demand for secondhand devices now far exceeds supply. Yet most phones still pass through many middlemen before reaching a buyer, adding cost at every step. NorthLadder’s platform connects sellers like Apple or Samsung directly with buyers like Amazon or Back Market. This enables better trade-in deals and lower resale prices, improving outcomes for consumers while increasing supply in an under-supplied market. We met Sandeep just after he led Careem’s largest business unit. Initially trying to recruit him for another portfolio company, he became the co-founder and CEO of NorthLadder, and we backed him. Alongside Co-Founder and COO Mihin Shah, the Northladder team pivoted their initial consumer-lending concept into a B2B infrastructure business for the second-hand phone market. Their ability to build beyond the original idea, and their conviction within a complex and technical space, reflects the adaptability we value in founders.

NowPay is an Egypt-based B2B FinTech platform offering corporate employees advance payments on salaries, along with a broader suite of financial wellness features such as bill payments, transfers, and BNPL. The team brings a product-first approach shaped by the founders’ technical experience at Microsoft, IBM, and Amazon. The company addresses a market where over half of Egypt’s workforce lives paycheck to paycheck, often turning to costly informal borrowing, and financial stress costs companies billions of dollars in productivity.
founders: Mostafa Ashour, Ahmed Sabry, Sherif Radi

description: Property Finder is the leading real estate classifieds platform in MENA. What began as a print magazine evolved into a digital-first property portal in 2007, now attracting over 14 million monthly visits across six regional markets. As the only regional VC in their shareholder base, we were drawn by Michael’s steady hand, conscientious leadership, and long-term vision.
beco_partnered: 2013 / Series A / Exited in 2024 (Early Stage) / 2026 Growth Stage

description: RemotePass is an HR platform, founded in the UAE, for onboarding, managing, and paying remote talent across the globe. When we backed the team, the company was a travel and expense tool for SMEs. Today, RemotePass enables companies to compliantly hire and pay contractors, direct employees, and EOR staff in over 150 countries, all through a unified interface. Distributed work has been a long-standing model in the region, particularly in the Gulf, given the deep talent pools in close proximity; a theme amplified by COVID as we see companies adopting this model from the outset, rather than only when they reach scale. RemotePass is a well-positioned partner for this rising theme, and today, BECO is both an investor and a happy customer.

description: RoundMenu was a UAE-based platform for restaurant discovery, table bookings, and food delivery, operating across 18 cities in MENA. The founding team saw an opportunity to digitize the outdated coupon and reservations industry in the region, offering restaurants a more dignified and dynamic alternative to group-buying deals.

SellAnyCar is a technology-driven platform that helps consumers sell their cars in under 30 minutes, offering instant online valuation, in-person inspection, and guaranteed purchase. The company is digitizing a historically fragmented and opaque industry across MENA, making used car sales faster, more transparent, and less stressful for both consumers and dealers.

description: Si-Ware makes the analysis of raw materials faster and cheaper by transforming lab-grade spectroscopy devices – traditionally large and expensive hardware – into portable, real-time sensing solutions. With the world’s first FT-IR spectrometer on a chip, the company enables accurate, field-ready analysis across food, feed, soil, and pharma using just a handheld device. We partnered with Si-Ware as the company shifted from a deep-tech IP house into a globally scalable, SaaS-enabled sensing platform. Si-Ware initially focused on the agriculture sector; today, the company is currently expanding to other verticals with Si-Ware’s proprietary chip technology.
founders: Youssri Helmy, Hisham Haddara, Dr. Bassam Saadany

description: Sirdab is a ‘Warehousing-as-a-Service’ platform in the logistics sector, operating in Saudi Arabia. After years of research and operating in first and last mile logistics, the team identified middle-mile warehousing as the most underserved, and potentially the most profitable, layer of the value chain. In a market where demand outstrips supply by 30-50%, Sirdab offers on-demand, tech-enabled warehousing and transport through a hybrid model of owned and partner-operated facilities. Having invested in Sirdab since seed, and co-led their Series A, we remain deeply impressed by the team’s execution, traction, and thoughtfulness around their vision.

Stream is a billing and payments platform built for Saudi Arabia, covering every stage of the payment lifecycle: invoicing, scheduling, payment processing through local rails, cashflow tracking, and reconciliation. The company has created a new category between payment processing and accounting software, owning the billing workflow layer that no local or global player currently addresses. Merchants see Stream as their billing system rather than a payment cost, a distinction that drives wallet share from 10% to 80% over time and creates deep operational stickiness through tokenized cards, payment history, and accounting integrations.

Supy is a back-of-house software platform for restaurants. Initially launched as a procurement and ordering tool, Supy evolved into a full-suite back-of-house SaaS platform. It helps restaurants manage inventory, procurement, accounting, and analytics with real-time control and deep visibility, addressing critical pain points in an industry dominated by outdated systems. We have been following Supy since its inception and have worked very closely with Dani and the team even prior to our investment. Despite having started with a focus on the GCC, they have quickly scaled internationally and are now live in 32 countries with hundreds of restaurant brands relying on Supy to power their back-of-house operations. The team’s deep domain expertise and obsession with building a world-class product have positioned them as a globally recognized company. Today we are Supy’s largest shareholder, and continue to work very closely in helping them execute on their vision to be the #1 back-of-house software provider for the F&B industry.
founders: Dani El-Zein, Ibrahim Bou Ncoula, Yazeed Bin Busayyis

description: SWVL began as a bus-hailing platform, offering a more reliable alternative to Egypt’s public and informal mass transport system. Over time, it evolved into a broader mobility infrastructure business, shifting focus to B2B and B2G offerings in the Gulf including corporate, school, and government fleet solutions. We backed SWVL, drawn by their strong early traction, experienced team, and novel solution to the challenges of public transport in emerging markets. Co-founder and CEO Mostafa Kandil brought deep and relevant experience from his time at Careem, launching eight markets from scratch, including rolling out four cities in a single day with just two weeks of preparation.
founders: Mostafa Kandil, Ahmed Sabbah, Mahmoud Nouh

description: Syarah is transforming how people buy cars in Saudi Arabia, making it fully digital, transparent, and hassle-free. From doorstep delivery to a 10-day return policy, Syarah lets buyers browse, finance, and purchase new or used cars entirely online. Backed by proprietary inspection and pricing systems, the company serves customers across the Kingdom through a mobile-first platform. The team’s focus on trust, user experience, and unlocking the underserved B2C car market drove our conviction in Syarah. It has since scaled into a national brand, trusted by millions.

description: Sympl is reimagining consumer finance in Egypt with the country’s first true “Save Now, Pay Later” (SNPL) platform. Built by the founding team behind ValU, Egypt’s leading consumer finance company, Sympl allows shoppers to split purchases into short-term, interest-free installments without pre-registration or lengthy onboarding. By removing friction at checkout, Sympl is unlocking affordability for the mass market, while driving conversion, ticket size, and frequency for merchants. We partnered with Sympl at seed, backing second-time founders with deep FinTech experience, merchant relationships, and the execution playbook to scale fast. In a market dominated by cash and expensive credit, Sympl’s card-based, no-interest model offers an elegant alternative for everyday spend, starting with fashion and expanding into broader retail.

Taager is a social e-commerce platform that connects online merchants with wholesalers, enabling anyone to start and scale their own social commerce business without upfront capital or inventory. The platform provides an end-to-end solution where merchants focus on marketing and customer acquisition while Taager handles product sourcing, warehousing, fulfillment, and logistics. Operating across Egypt, Saudi Arabia, UAE and Iraq, Taager is currently serving thousands of social sellers, from university students to ambitious entrepreneurs. We first backed Taager when their operations were primarily in Egypt. Long before Saudi Arabia’s prominence on the regional tech stage, the team had the foresight to enter the Gulf and saw remarkable traction as one of the region’s first movers, expanding quietly but effectively across borders while staying grounded in merchant needs. Taager continues to expand across MENA, realizing its ambition to become the region’s category leader.
founders: Mohammed Elhorishy, Ismail Omar, Abdelrahman Sherief, Ahmed Ismail

description: Tabby is a consumer fintech platform that enables shoppers to split their purchases into flexible, interest-free payments online and in-store. The company partners with thousands of merchants across the GCC and Egypt, serving millions of active users and processing billions in annual transaction volume. Through its “buy now, pay later” and shopping discovery app, Tabby has become a core part of the regional retail ecosystem, helping merchants increase conversion and retention while offering consumers greater affordability and transparency. In 2024, Tabby acquired our portfolio company Tweeq in an all stock transaction. Today, Tabby stands at a $4.5B valuation and continues to anchor MENA’s fintech ecosystem, proving the depth of local fintech opportunity when executed with discipline and insight.

Tenderd is a construction tech company transforming how contractors manage and rent heavy equipment across the Middle East region, with ambitions to grow globally. Tenderd combines local insight with a global product mindset, led by a second-time founder, Arjun, who returned to the region after building an AI startup in Silicon Valley. The platform began as a managed marketplace for underutilized machinery and has since evolved into a full-stack, AI-powered fleet management system serving the region’s largest contractors. When we backed Arjun, we were drawn to his experience as a founder, product intuition, and unwavering ambition to digitize one of the region’s most operationally intensive and under-digitized industries.
co_investors: Y Combinator, Paul Graham, Peter Thiel, A.P. Moller Holding

description: Thndr is a digital trading platform on a mission to democratize access to capital markets across the Middle East. The company offers a mobile-first experience for trading stocks, mutual funds, and fixed income products, making investing simple, intuitive, and commission-free.
co_investors: Prosus, Tiger Global, Y Combinator, Endeavor Catalyst

description: Trofee is a live shopping marketplace enabling sellers across the Middle East to reach highly engaged audiences, starting with a focus on collectibles and fashion. The platform enables sellers to livestream shows which buyers tune into to bid on and purchase consumer goods ranging from sneakers to collectibles such as sports memorabilia and pokemon cards. We partnered with Trofee, impressed by the founders’ deep domain expertise and clear vision of wanting to build a category leader in what is otherwise a whitespace today. Our investment in Trofee fits squarely within our Consumer Tech thesis, targeting a fast growing sector in MENA which is characterised by a high propensity to spend with a community-based approach and leveraging the region’s high mobile phone penetration.

Tweeq is a KSA-based digital wallet and neo-bank offering seamless money management for individuals and SMEs across MENAP. Founded by a veteran team from Al Rajhi, FAB, STC, and NBB, Tweeq is building a mobile-first platform with features like multi-currency accounts, instant payments, and smart budgeting. We invested in Tweeq in 2021 due to their strong regulatory progress, a clear GTM via university channels, and deep FinTech experience. In 2024, Tabby – the leading regional BNPL platform acquired Tweeq in an all stock transaction.
founders: Saeed Albuhairi, Abdulaziz Almalki, Mohammad Faheem, and Abdullah AlOtaibi

description: Vectara helps enterprises build AI-native applications that understand meaning – starting with best-in-class search, grounded in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Vectara’s platform allows developers and product teams to embed accurate, secure, and multilingual semantic search with speed, observability, and deployment flexibility. We backed a highly experienced team with both operational depth and acute product-focus in the generative AI landscape. As data volume, complexity, and urgency continue to outpace conventional tools, Vectara’s approach, real-time comprehension at retrieval, represents a foundational shift in how enterprises handle information retrieval.
founders: Amr Awadallah, Amin Ahmad, Tallat Shafaat

description: Vezeeta was founded in Egypt with a vision to bring structure, transparency, and scale to MENA’s fragmented healthcare ecosystem. The company began as a doctor booking platform but quickly evolved into a digital healthcare booking platform and practice management software, powering millions of patient-doctor interactions, digitizing clinic workflows, and enabling pharma, diagnostics, and insurance integrations.

Wahed is the world’s first halal robo-advisor, offering sharia-compliant investment portfolios through a low-cost, mobile-first platform. Today, Wahed serves over 400,000 customers across the US, UK, GCC, and Southeast Asia.

Founded in 2015 as one of the world’s first AI meeting assistants, Wrappup was an AI-powered productivity app that leveraged speech recognition to make it easy to record, tag, and summarize conversations, saving users from the chaos of manual note-taking. In 2018, Wrappup was acquired by Voicera which was later acquired by Cisco.
